findings.claim: The production compose file requires `FRF_ENTITY_WATCH_CHECKPOINT_KEY` unconditionally, contradicting the gateway validation/docs that require it only when CDC is enabled and breaking non-CDC deployments.
findings.evidence: compose.yml adds `ENTITY_WATCH_CHECKPOINT_KEY: "${FRF_ENTITY_WATCH_CHECKPOINT_KEY:?FRF_ENTITY_WATCH_CHECKPOINT_KEY is required}"`, while `crates/frf-gateway/src/config/validation.rs` enforces the key only inside `if self.cdc_enabled { ... }` and `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` describes the variable as required for CDC.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the compose requirement conditional via the CDC/full deployment profile or provide a separate CDC compose overlay; do not use `${VAR:?}` in the base service unless the key is mandatory for every gateway start.

findings.claim: The broker watch adapter turns a different-tenant entity event into a terminal permission error before the app-layer tenant filter can safely ignore it, so a cross-tenant event on the shared entity channel can kill authorized watches instead of being filtered.
findings.evidence: `BrokerEntityTypeWatchSource::subscribe` returns `PortError::PermissionDenied("entity watch envelope tenant mismatch")` when `mutation.tenant_id != envelope.channel.tenant_id`, but acceptance A requires other tenants to receive no protected payload and the application stream code has explicit filtering for `delivery.mutation.tenant_id != producer.request.tenant_id` only after the adapter emits a delivery.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not reject well-formed entity mutations solely because their tenant differs from the channel tenant; pass the delivery to the use case for tenant filtering, or make the broker channel partitioning guarantee per-tenant and document/enforce it at publish time instead of terminating subscribers.
